events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
The cancellation fee stands only through NS-0's driver-cancellation branch: the driver cancelled at 12:09:25 (7 min 25 s after acceptance) and asserted the rider was a no-show, which puts the case under NS-1/NS-2 [F3][NS-0]. Cancelled_by = driver and the driver's own statement claims non-appearance, so the fee's validity turns on NS-1's three conditions [F12][NS-1].

NS-1 (i) is met but (ii) fails. The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15, so an arrival was confirmed by driver_tap [F5][NS-1]. But at that moment the GPS put him 600 m from the pickup point, and his closest approach for the whole trip was 599 m — he was never inside the 200 m zone [F5][F1]. NS-1 (ii) requires the tap to be made while GPS shows the driver at the pickup location; it is therefore not satisfied [NS-1].

NS-1 (iii) fails as well. claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 while 600 m from the pickup point, so requirement (ii) of NS-1 fails: at the moment of the tap the GPS record does not place the driver at the pickup location.

NS-1 requirement (iii) also fails: after tapping "I'm Here" the driver spent 0 seconds within 200 m of the pickup point, and the driver's closest approach for the whole trip was 599 m, so there was no continuous 3-minute wait at the pickup before cancelling.

The platform itself never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), corroborating that no valid arrival occurred — the only arrival signal is the driver's own button press 600 m away.
With NS-1 (ii) and (iii) unmet, the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full to the rider; the fee appears on the record as charged.
Because the driver pressed "I'm Here" while the GPS showed him outside the pickup area (600 m > 200 m), the case additionally warrants flag_account for abuse of the cancellation/waiting button.

The driver's written statement that he waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records and is therefore not relied on; the record shows he was stationary 600 m away for the 3 min 30 s before cancelling.

The driver's in-app message "I'm here already" at 12:06 was sent while he was 600 m from the pickup, and the rider's reply at 12:07 confirms the rider was at the pickup point with no car present; both are consistent with the GPS record.
The dispute is timely: the complaint is filed in this case immediately after the 12:09:25 cancellation, well within the 30-day window for cancellation-fee disputes.

The driver's 90-day record already contains one upheld no-show dispute, so this second no-show cancellation is a repeat of the same conduct and supports the account-review flag as an additional action, not as the basis of the finding.

weaknesses: The rider sent no message before 12:06 showing where she was; the first rider message is a reply at 12:07 (F9), so there is no pre-tap chat evidence of her waiting, only the GPS/timeline record.

The driver did tap "I'm Here" and did wait 3 min 30 s in one place (F2, F5); the other side will argue that the 3-minute wait condition was satisfied and that the only defect is the location, which they may attribute to GPS error.

No traffic or weather fact is cited by either side here (F13–F15 not relied on); there is no independent third-party record (e.g., driver_arrived_at) confirming the rider's presence at pickup, only absence of any record of the driver there (F4).
The $6.61 figure is a flat published fee (F6) and the rider's own profile shows no prior disputes (F16), so nothing in the profile supports a severe-conduct finding beyond the single flag.

claims.assertion: The cancellation fee of $6.61 stands only if the driver's no-show claim satisfies NS-1, and the record shows his "I'm Here" tap was made 600 m from the pickup point, so the NS-1 (ii) location requirement is not met.

The platform never recorded the driver arriving at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and his closest approach during the whole trip was 599 m, so he was never within 200 m of the pickup point at any time.

The driver was stationary for 3 min 30 s (12:05:55–12:09:25) but 600 m from the pickup point, so the NS-1 (iii) requirement of continuous waiting inside the pickup zone is not satisfied; time waited elsewhere does not count.
The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, so the system records win over the statement.
Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are not all satisfied, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded in full to the rider rather than treating this as a no-show.
Any refund must follow NS-7's form (Ryde voucher within the 30-day window), the disputed item being the $6.61 cancellation fee shown at F6 and F3.

The driver's "I'm Here" tap at a GPS position outside the pickup zone (600 m > 200 m) is exactly the situation NS-2 attaches a possible account flag to, which the driver does not contest; he asks only that it be weighed with his profile of a 6.3-year account, 4.67 rating and 464 trips in 90 days.

weaknesses: Two system records defeat NS-1 for the driver: F1 (closest approach 599 m, never within 200 m) and F5 ("I'm Here" tapped 600 m from the pickup, 0 s spent within 200 m afterwards).
F2 shows the driver stationary 3 min 30 s at 600 m from the pickup, which reads as the arrival/waiting button being pressed while not at the pick-up location — the abuse pattern NS-2 flags.
F8 (12:06 driver: "I'm here already, silver Toyota Altis, please come out") is contemporaneous with F5 and cannot be squared with the driver's actual position.
F17 records a prior upheld no-show dispute within 90 days, so the NS-2 flag request is likely to be treated as repeat conduct rather than an isolated lapse.
F9 (rider: "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?") is a rider message before cancellation that corroborates the GPS position rather than the driver's account.

Not contested — F3 shows cancellation at 12:09:25 and this case is filed in the same window, so NS-7's 30-day condition is met and the $6.61 refund should be issued as a Ryde voucher rather than cash.
